thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 PAGE: gpu-pool-usw2-spot reported 95% queue growth and autoscaler errors (scale_limit_hit). Marked P1 for oncall. @Dave (oncall) please ack and start bridge if needed.

Dave (oncall): acked. jumping in. what's the customer impact? any 5xx spike?

Jane (Support): I see increased error rates for /v1/generate and a few timeouts in the last 3m. Small number of customers (~8) on dedicated plans reporting increased latency >10s. No 5xx mass outage yet.

Amy (prod-eng): autoscaler logs show repeated failures to provision spot gpus: "insufficient capacity" + quota errors. fallback_policy tried to route to dedicated but dedicated pools are near capacity. queue length spiked from 120 -> 950 in ~6m.

Luis (SRE): digging into autoscaler controller logs now, tailing: 
```
E 2026-03-15T12:01:42Z controller.go:322 provisioner: failed to allocate node: spotProvider: quota exceeded, preemptionChain=3
W 2026-03-15T12:02:10Z autoscaler.go:88 scale_limit_hit: reached pool.max_nodes=200 for pool=gpu-spot-usw2
```
Looks like preemptible churn plus max_nodes cap.

Marcus (infra): confirmed spot eviction events spiking from cloud provider side. We hit a preemption chain: nodes keep being replaced and scale backfilling fails. provider status link: https://console.cloud/ops/evictions?pool=gpu-spot-usw2

Dave (oncall): plan? do we route to CPU fallback models? that will increase latency but keep clients live.

Amy (prod-eng): propose emergency mitigation steps: 1) enable emergency_burst_pool (reserved warm nodes) to accept critical traffic; 2) enable queue-priority header prioritization to drain high-SLA requests; 3) temporarily raise pool.max_nodes to 300 if quota allows; 4) apply backpressure for low-priority batches (reject with 429).

infra-bot: running check: current quota for GPUs in project: 220 used / 300 quota. preemptible quota available: 30.

Marcus (infra): we can bump max_nodes in config, but cloud quota needs increase; raising to 300 will exceed GPU quota unless we request emergency quota. that takes time. alternative: evict non-prod workloads from dedicated pools and reassign to c4-cpu nodes.

Luis (SRE): I can run a targeted eviction for noncritical training jobs (label: team!=prod). command I will run: 
```
kubectl get pods -l team!=prod -n gpu-jobs -o name | xargs -r kubectl delete -n gpu-jobs
```
That should free ~18 GPUs within 2-3 minutes.

Amy (prod-eng): good. also flip routing to fallback host pool for low-latency customers only if they have fallback flag enabled. send a config change to the router: 
```
PATCH /config/route
{ "route": "prefer:dedicated, fallback:cpu-small, prioritize_header": "x-priority" }
```

deploy-bot: applied quick patch to routing (id: r-5632) to prioritize x-priority header.

Jane (Support): I'm messaging impacted customers with a short note: "We're experiencing degraded performance in GPU-backed endpoints due to provider-side preemptions; we've activated mitigations and prioritized your requests. We'll update in 30m." Any specific SLA language to include?

Dave (oncall): good. include that we're rerouting critical requests and throttling lower-priority workloads. escalate to incident commander if we see >20% error rate or prolonged queue > 30m.

Luis (SRE): autoscaler still logs backlog. I'm enabling a temporary override to ignore scale_limit_hit for 5m to allow emergency bursts (manual throttle). running: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/autoscaler OVERRIDE_SCALE_LIMIT=true --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

infra-bot: OVERRIDE_SCALE_LIMIT applied; note: this may attempt to provision beyond configured safeguards. Monitoring provisioning events.

Marcus (infra): cloud provider is still returning sporadic "preemption_chain" spikes. we've requested emergency quota increase (ticket #Q-8899). response ETA ~45m.

Dave (oncall): immediate next actions: Luis evict non-prod, Amy confirm routing changes, Marcus monitor quota ticket, Jane keep customers posted. assign owners and update #incident-docs.

Amy (prod-eng): evictions completed, freed 22 GPUs. queue length dropping from 950 -> 310 in last 4m. latency for high-priority requests back to ~1.2s.

Jane (Support): updating customers: "we freed capacity by pausing non-critical workloads and routing your requests to priority pools. Expect continued improvement; we'll follow up when quota request resolves."

Luis (SRE): provisioning events now showing successful node launches, but many are preemptible and have short lifespans. still seeing some churn but autoscaler stable for now.

Dave (oncall): nice work. lowering severity to P2 for now but keep bridge open for 30m. capture action items: 1) runbook gap: add preemption_chain detection + auto-evict non-prod logic; 2) evaluate reserved burst capacity for critical customers; 3) improve fallback routing to avoid total reliance on spare dedicated.

Amy (prod-eng): I'll own runbook updates and a postmortem. setting follow-up to review quota handling and autoscaler safeguards.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=degraded->stabilizing, duration=~24m, next update at +30m.

Dave (oncall): closing bridge in 28m, leaving paging on. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
